cross_cutting_rules: No shared name, field, encoding, or visual representation establishes semantic equivalence.
Equivalence requires an explicit definition, traceable transformation, and behavioral validation.
A phase transition and a behavioral classification are not interchangeable merely because both use the word 'changing'.
Canonical temporal phase, visualization oscillator phase, numerical simulation time, and acoustic signal parameters must retain distinct definitions.
No normalization, conversion, or canonical-authority decision follows from shared terminology alone.
Producer provenance, input conditions, and semantic definition must accompany every generated state representation.
Matching field names do not establish matching meanings.
gate_2_questions: Are the two Yao criteria equivalent? — No (established)
Is ternary_state safe as shared cross-generation field? — No (established)
Is enriched direction semantically validated? — Unresolved
Can the files be reconciled without losing meaning? — Not established

Select canonical cross-system representation — Not authorized / unresolved
completion_criterion: Every disputed representation has an identified producer, a recoverable definition, a known set of consumers, and an evidence-backed statement of what transformations are permitted or prohibited.
